title: the row a callback's capability read charges the caller is the same nominal row a Layer for that capability subtracts, so the program compiles and runs
notes: specification/requirements.mdx, 'Inference': 'Requirement inference MUST be transitive through ordinary calls.' The acceptance half of `a-callback-capability-escapes-the-top-level-check`, and the reason both halves exist: the refusal case can only show that SOMETHING is charged, while this one shows WHAT. If the callback's read charged nothing, this program would still compile and would then panic at run time with `capability 'Reader' was not provided`; if it charged some other key, `Layer.succeed(Reader, service)` would not subtract it and the program would be refused for an unsatisfied capability. Only running it under a layer that provides exactly Reader distinguishes those three outcomes, and running it is the only way to assert a row on the Go fork at all — its CompileResult protocol carries no rows, so behaviour under an exact layer is the assertion. THIS CASE IS ALSO THE OVER-CORRECTION GUARD FOR TWO RULES AT ONCE, which is why it is an `output` case in an area mostly made of refusals. First, the callback rule: the fix that charges a callback's row to its caller must NOT charge a `Layer.provide` computation the capabilities its own layer provides — that would republish to the caller exactly what the provide site satisfies, and every program in the area would become unsatisfiable. Line 15 is that shape, and it turns red if the exclusion is dropped. Second, the top-level rule: `a-top-level-capability-read-is-rejected` charges a read at module scope, and a read reachable FROM module scope through a provide computation must stay accepted — a rule that could not tell those apart would turn this case red rather than passing quietly. Two keys are read rather than one because a single-element `map` is satisfied by a callback invoked once for the wrong reason; two ordered outputs show the callback ran per element with the capability available each time. WHAT THIS DELIBERATELY DOES NOT PIN: it does not claim the row is `[Reader]` by inspecting it — no corpus expectation can read a row on either backend — only that whatever is charged is subtracted by exactly this layer, which is the observable form of the same statement. VERIFIED LOAD-BEARING, not assumed: mutating the second declared stdout line from `ZOE` to `ZOO` turns the case red on BOTH backends with the stdout diff printed, and the expectation was restored byte-identically (sha256 d97a859aa016f8193caae5decf6eb3b92f3b7616a8c155c9deb498e87169bf0b before and after). An `output` case is mutated on its stdout because that is where its whole claim lives — the program having run at all, and having read the capability on each element.
